title: Replace Words
summary: Given a dictionary of roots and a sentence, replace each derivative word in the sentence with the shortest root that forms it.
statement: Given a dictionary of roots and a sentence, replace each derivative word in the sentence with the shortest root that forms it. If a derivative word can be formed by more than one root, select the root with the shortest length. Return the modified sentence.
constraints: Dictionary roots and sentence words contain lowercase letters; words are separated by single spaces.
Replace each word with its shortest dictionary prefix, if one exists.
hints: Only prefixes matter, and the first matching length is optimal.
Store roots in a set and scan each word’s prefixes from shortest to longest.
For each word, stop at the first prefix in roots; otherwise keep the word.
Checking prefix lengths in increasing order directly enforces the shortest-root rule.
editorial: Checking prefix lengths in increasing order directly enforces the shortest-root rule.

arguments: the cattle was rattled by the battery
tests.expected: the cat was rat by the bat
tests.explanation: The derivatives cattle, rattled, and battery use their shortest matching roots.
Every word beginning with a becomes a; the other words remain unchanged.
